response: The clustering is getting closer but still has key problems. The "Diverse Astronomical Observations Survey" and "Diverse Astrophysical Phenomena Studies" clusters are still catch-alls mixing galactic/extragalactic topics (galaxy morphology, star-forming galaxies, ISM), solar/stellar topics (sunspot tracking, chromospheric signals), and high-energy topics (supernovae, FRBs) — these should be separated into their proper subject areas rather than lumped together. There is still no dedicated solar and stellar astrophysics cluster; papers on solar active regions, stellar magnetic fields, chromospheric physics, stellar atmospheres, and stellar abundances are scattered across "Magnetic fields astrophysical waves," "Astrophysical Data Analysis Methods," and the catch-all clusters and should be consolidated into one. Similarly, galactic and extragalactic papers (galaxy kinematics, galaxy scaling relations, ISM, star formation in galaxies) should form a single coherent cluster rather than being split across multiple groups.
